description:
Root-cause spike complete. The accumulated dirty prototype is evidence, not a landing candidate.

Goal
A source callable construction owns one runtime callable object and one producer-correlated member dispatch plan. Exact calls may bypass that object and use a private executable ABI. Every source CallClosure target, whether locally constructed or received generically, obeys the public callable ABI: boxed arguments, self, continuation; its result form is Absent, one boxed ValueRef, or Diverges.

First loss
Semantic analysis already preserves the correct authority in CallableFlowFact keyed by local producer: function, lexical captures, and each surface-to-resolution edge with capture and argument semantic mappings. Root backend packaging discards the producer boundary by flattening those edges into root-wide BackendCallableEntry rows, then asks one shared TransportPosition to choose a resolved_entry. A shared generic consumer legitimately receives multiple members, so no position-level entry stamp can represent the answer.

Runtime proof
Construction values already store a generated callable-boundary shim, not wrapper_fn. Zero-capture singletons and capturing closures both use the shim. The shim owns boxed args plus self plus cont, extracts captures, and tail-calls a private Direct wrapper. Exact closure calls bypass indirect CallClosure and retain narrow executable ABI.

The dirty spike makes interpreter member dispatch work but regresses previously-green native Range scalar and Range3. LLDB on the Enum.take crash proves the same return-seam error: fz_closure_get_capture_ref receives a runtime code address as continuation self because a one-word public result invoked a continuation compiled for two private result lanes plus self. Capture loading is the victim, not the source.

Authority model
- CallableFlowFact is the semantic authority for one producer construction and its member dispatch.
- The construction wrapper catalog owns producer, retained logical captures, member selection, semantic input mappings, and each member private input/return layout.
- TransportLayout is one component-solved fact containing structural shape plus physical carrier. Carrier is an independent monotone join, not a recursive post-hoc scan.
- The wrapper public return contract contains only Absent, BoxedValueRef, or Diverges. It does not copy a member structural ShapeId.
- Each member target owns its private return layout. One target-to-public adapter boxes it.
- CallReturnFlow owns public-to-caller delivery. Every indirect call uses one generic adapter; tail forwarding is allowed only when public and caller return forms agree.
- Construction identity is consumed at allocation to choose the shim. Once materialized, the runtime ValueRef code pointer and environment are the authority. Identity is not propagated beside the value.

Required implementation
1. Preserve producer-keyed construction facts from CallableFlowFact through root packaging. Generate one multi-member wrapper and dispatch plan per construction.
2. Materialize a first-class producer once with the construction shim and one ValueRef per retained logical capture. Exact direct-only values remain structural and allocation-free.
3. Make transport solve one TransportLayout per canonical component. Remove ExecutableRuntimeDemand.runtime_carriers, recursive transport_carrier_required, and duplicate position_shapes/transport_shapes storage rather than compensating for missing carrier propagation.
4. Replace wrapper return_layout chosen from the first nonempty member with a public return form. Keep private member return layouts only in the target-to-public adapter.
5. Make every indirect ClosureCall select its continuation adapter from the public return form, never from recovered construction identity or a target return position. Consolidate boxed Return and Deliver adapters.
6. Delete call-time construction repair: construction_wrapper_positions fixed-point propagation, BackendSemanticInputLayout.construction, RuntimeConstruction, native per-variable carried-boundary recovery, interpreter FnId/construction fallbacks used to choose return ABI, and target-derived closure return selection.
7. Encode allocation identity directly in MakeFnRef/MakeClosure or look it up by identity_fn; do not require NativeBody.callable_value_boundaries as a parallel per-variable authority. Unknown generic callables remain valid public-ABI values; opaque compiler callables remain ABI-conforming traps.
8. Remove the temporary FnId 16 eprintln/import before gates. Pare back prototype-only re-derivations rather than layering fixes over them.

Proof
- Model tests assert one producer construction with all members, stable member selection, one component TransportLayout, and no call-time identity side channel.
- Enum predicate/take/drop/split interp, JIT, run, and build.
- Range scalar, Range2 first accumulator, Range3 halt/suspend interp and JIT.
- Existing operator-ref reducer, opaque escaped lambda, continuation capture, spawn/destructor, and direct-only no-allocation contracts.
- cargo test --lib and cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings.

Carrier proof
Range2 identified the exact first carrier loss without a special-case hypothesis. At the root callsite span 286..293, resume entry 1, value 3 has RuntimeDemand::Whole. Its solved component contains the selected executable return and the root ResumePayload, structural ShapeId 12, but both position branches hardcode carrier false, so the final layout is Absent. Component-wide joining cannot repair false seeds. Carrier must be projected from the authoritative demand of every component member, then joined once; result/return/resume position kinds do not define carrier semantics.

Public return seam proof
The remaining Range2 trace proved that private member return and public callable return are currently invalidly equated before native lowering. jobs/artifact.rs call_return_flow treats a ClosureCall target hint as CallTarget::Local(member): Deliver names the member ExecutableReturn as payload, and Return compares that member return against caller payload/return to classify Tail. Backend preserves this flow even when runtime invocation is indirect and member selection belongs to the construction wrapper. A private member return such as RawAtom plus ValueRef and the public boxed ValueRef result therefore enter one transport component; broad carrier joins only move the mismatch. Construction closure calls need an explicit public callable-return source/layout keyed by their boundary or callsite. Member target-to-public adaptation ends at that seam; public-to-caller adaptation begins there. Only exact direct closure calls may use member ExecutableReturn and its tail equality.

Carrier authority correction
The first direct-demand carrier redesign was falsified. Non-Ignore RuntimeDemand means the semantic value is live; it does not mean the private ABI is boxed. Structural shape already supplies private lanes. Treating every demanded ExecutableReturn as ValueRef caused wrapper target-to-public adaptation to reinterpret raw member values as tagged boxes, producing Nil. Carrier must be an explicit physical seam anchor joined through the transport component: first-class callable publication/materialization and the public callable return seam anchor ValueRef; ordinary private executable returns and direct values remain structural unless their own boundary anchors otherwise. Resume/Return payloads inherit public boxing only through equality with the public seam, never from position kind or generic liveness.

Exact-call return proof
Range2 LLDB proves the first malformed handoff is Fn2 -> Fn56: Fn2 returns private RawInt 3, while Fn56 declares ValueRef. Fn56 and Fn99 preserve raw 3 as if boxed; Fn92 later calls fz_unbox_int(0x3) and observes Nil. The runtime callable is correct: Fn39 MakeFnRef(Fn35) resolves construction 0 to generated boundary 0 and callable_wrapper_0 Fn37. Tuple projection, tuple_field_params, stale-GC, construction selection, and public-wrapper-return hypotheses were falsified.
The bad edge is an exact closure-call fast path inside the wrapper member. Native lowering correctly knows the exact private target but closure_call_return_position deliberately returns None whenever construction identity is present. delivered_call_continuation then falls back to the public ResumePayload and creates a ValueRef continuation instead of decoding the exact target ExecutableReturn RawInt and adapting it to the public payload. Construction identity is therefore being used at call time to suppress the private source ABI, contradicting the model that identity is consumed only at allocation.
Implementation must remove this call-time construction-dependent return selection. An exact direct closure call always takes its source contract from the exact target ExecutableReturn; its continuation adapts that private result to the public payload/caller contract. Indirect calls remain public ABI. Remove the redundant construction parameter/branch rather than adding a boxing fallback or changing Fn56/Fn92. Tail forwarding remains legal only for physically identical private/caller contracts.
title: fz-k22: preserve producer callable constructions behind one public indirect ABI
